information.description:
Special Agents lead small armies of Netwatch officers, or helm larger investigations that requires real talent. They have some of the best netrunning cyberware available, are extremely skilled, and can be a true menace in a fight. Stay far away.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Netwatch).

description.value: Master hackers who put themselves at risk as they jack into cyberspace to download secrets and infiltrate networks.
Throwing hands, does not ignore half armor.

A .42 caliber, six-shot, semiautomatic, double-action, Power-class revolver crafted with the classic Malorian traits – heavy, reliable, and packed with firepower. Although Malorian has been faring worse on the market than its competitors in recent years, the Overture is still an iconic, high-quality weapon that can be found on the streets.

Cost: 2,500eb (Very Expensive)

Class: EQ Very Heavy Pistol • Skill: Handgun • Range: Long Barrel Pistol

Damage: 4d6 • Capacity: 6 • ROF: 1 • Hands: 1

Alt. Firing Modes: None

Concealable: No

Slots: 2 • Attachments: Pistol Long Barrel, Power Rebuild • Mods: None

Special Features: Incompatible with Capacity modifying Attachments. When using this weapon to make an Aimed Shot, it deals 1d6 additional damage (5d6). When rolling for damage with this weapon, any damage die which land on a 1 are re-rolled until they result in a higher value.

Range: Long Barrel Pistol
Pre-installed: Pistol Long Barrel, Power Rebuild (effects already included in these stats)

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Weapons > Weapon Catalog).

Cost: 2,500eb (Very Expensive) ♦ Install: Hospital

Humanity Loss: 14 (4d6)

Replaces the user’s upper spine and neck area with an extra block of nervous connections and reinforced musculature.

Borgware. Internal Body Cyberware. Requires Neuroport, but does not take up a Neuralware Option Slot. Requires 3 Internal Body Option Slots. Provides 4 additional Neuralware Option Slots. The user is also now immune to the effect and bonus damage of the Crushed Windpipe and Whiplash Critical Injuries. Only one Advanced Neural Link may be installed. This cyberware counts as a Cyberspine for the purposes of drug or cyberware based effects or requirements.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 0, provides 4

Foundry notes:

  • Typed as Neuralware so its 4 extra Neuralware slots are usable: the sheet only offers install targets whose cyberware type matches the option being installed. Its 3 Internal Body Option Slots are not tracked, and its size is 0 because Corgo says it takes no Neuralware slot.
  • Counts as Borgware for Maximum Humanity Loss; the sheet doesn't track that, so apply it by hand.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Borgware).
A cybernetical replacement arm. Comes with a free hand.
The arm and installed options are not affected by EMP effects.

Cost: 5,000eb (Luxury) ♦ Install: Hospital

Humanity Loss: 14 (4d6)

This rare, usually Netwatch-exclusive ‘ware replaces the user's upper back, rear skull, and parts of their arms with a heap of top-of-the-line processors and hardware connections to make you into a walking, talking netrunning station. If you see someone sporting this, run.

Borgware. Requires a Neuroport Cyberdeck Port and paired Cyberarms. Takes up 3 Neuralware Option Slots and 2 Cyberarm Option Slots on both of the paired Cyberarms. Increases the Neuroport Cyberdeck Port's range to 80m/yds for Quickhacking, and to 40m/yds for accessing Non-Neuroport Net Architectures.

Also functions as two installations of Ex-Disk, and a single installation of Self-Ice. Allows the user to install Bodyweight Coatings as if they were a FBC. Any Overheat quickhack applied to the user has its damage reduced to Mildly on Fire (2 HP damage a turn) due to mobile cooling systems. This cyberware cannot be concealed, and is rather noticeable without a layer of clothing to somewhat obscure it.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 3

Foundry notes:

  • Typed as Neuralware, taking its 3 Neuralware slots; the 2 Cyberarm slots it needs in each arm are not tracked by the sheet.
  • Counts as Borgware for Maximum Humanity Loss; the sheet doesn't track that, so apply it by hand.

Cost: 500eb (Expensive) ♦ Install: Clinic

Humanity Loss: 3 (1d6)

Facilitates superconductivity in connective cyberware circuitry.

Neuralware. Any of the user’s Synapse Burnout Quickhacks can now inflict Critical Injuries, rolling on the Head Location Critical Injury Table when they occur. Additionally, any of the user’s Overheat Quickhacks now deal damage at the start of an enemies turn instead of the end.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Clinic
Option Slots: uses 1

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).

Cost: 500eb (Expensive) ♦ Install: Hospital

Humanity Loss: 14 (4d6)

The modern Kerenzikov takes the place of the now defunct Reflex Co-Processor to help reduce the strain on the user's Neuroport.

Neuralware. The user can now dodge Ranged Attacks if they could not do so already, and gain a +2 bonus to Checks for noticing Ambushes.

NOTE: Credit to Infernox_Ratchet for the basis of this item.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 1

Foundry notes:

  • Replaces the core system's Kerenzikov; use this one instead of the core item.
  • The +2 is on Perception and situational, because it only applies to noticing an Ambush: tick it in the roll dialog.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).

Cost: 500eb (Expensive)

If you want to stay in the game, you’re going to need a boost.

Kerenzikov Cyberware Enhancement. The Kerenzikov now counts as Speedware and also provides a +2 bonus to initiative at all times. Only 1 piece of Speedware can be installed at a time.

Enhances: Kerenzikov
Option Slots: 0 (Cyberware Enhancement)

Foundry notes:

  • The +2 initiative isn't automated from an upgrade; add it to the Kerenzikov as an Active Effect (bonuses.initiative) or apply it by hand.
